    The additive category Q of Proposition 2.3 #

    Given a vector space W with maps q_i : W → D_i (i ∈ J), let K_i ⊆ W be the intersection of the kernels ker q_j over j ∈ J with j ≤ i (for i ∈ J this is ker q_i when the q_i are compatible). The functor Φ_W on the interval category sends Y ↦ W, P i ↦ K_i and A i ↦ 0; a morphism between Y, P-intervals acts by its value at * times the inclusion. The category Q is the additive envelope of the one-point extension of the interval category by Φ_W: it adjoins an object L with Q(L, Y) = W, Q(L, P i) = K_i and no morphisms into L (Step 2 of the proof of Proposition 2.3).
